text: RWB-S2-E2017-APP is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-017: the thirteen legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC13, the eleven exception paths, the ten business rules, the overrides form, the regenerate operation, the review action, the send and their decision records stay with RWB-P5-E2017-APP and RWB-P5-E2017-CON in rwb-document, and this story writes eight criteria of its own that test only the treatment leg of SCR-14. The legacy test cases are kept in the order the work package lists and their Covers keep the legacy AC number in brackets.
why: One legacy capability cannot have two owners of the same criteria, and the work package carries the key as Split (rework) with an empty acs list for this story and RWB-P5-E2017-CON as its only contract dependency.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 7, 12, 13, 15 and 16; Template and Rules sections R5.4, R5.7 and R7.2 s7; work package B2-S2-019 story line for RWB-S2-E2017-APP; RWB-P5-E2017-APP sections 1 and 7.
applied_in: Story sections 1, 7 and 16; section 18 story rows; fragment acs and tcs
confirm: The P5 slice owner confirms that RWB-P5-E2017-APP carries the thirteen legacy criteria and the actions word for word.
impact: Low: the split follows the ownership map and the work package, and no legacy criterion is lost.

text: The panel is published as the optional documentPanel property of the treatment read API-S2-002 at the same major version, with treatmentApproved, treatmentOpen, treatmentType, productGroup, canGenerate, canSend, blockerMessageId, blockerDetail, setComplete, setAvailable, an expectedSet array and a documents array. The set is read on one REST hop from the set operation of RWB-P5-E2017-CON with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and a fake; no document row is read, no table or column is added, and the names and members are this story's design until the contract freeze.
why: No source gives the treatment read a panel, an action state or a set summary, and the legacy composed the panel in one process and one schema, so the read has to be published somewhere for the screen to bind to; the treatment read is the only surface SCR-14 already uses and the document set belongs to the document service.
read: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (no set or action field) and T-A.1 (four treatment operations); legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 4, 12 and 15; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13 and R7.2 s12.
confirm: The owner of RWB-S2-E3001-CON and of RWB-P5-E2017-CON with the solution architect at the wave 2 contract freeze.
impact: Medium: a change of the property names or of the set operation changes the client and its fake and no criterion.

text: DP-03 is applied as a read on this slice. The approval fact the panel shows is the reference in DF-TRT-003 to the local decision_record the approval story wrote through the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library with decision code D6.4; this story resolves that reference and writes no record, because every record of the actions the panel enables (the correction and the send) is written by rwb-document and none by rwb-treatment. The H row the pattern table adds is a platform capability the service template carries.
why: The pattern list of the work package carries DP-03, while the legacy story's only decision-log writes are the correction and the send, both of which the target places in the document service; writing a second record of the same action in the treatment service would duplicate the ledger entry the legacy has exactly once.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 4, 8 (BR4, BR9) and 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03; RWB-P5-E2017-APP sections 1 and 12.3 (the D6.4 record of a correction and of a send is the document service's).
confirm: The P7 ledger owner and the rwb-document tech lead confirm that the key's records stay with P5.
impact: Low: no second record exists, and the gate reads the one the approval story wrote.

text: DP-07 adds the C row RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the H row RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, neither of which the work package's lists hold: the metadata keeps Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E2017-CON only, the story builds against the reference-data fake until the contract publishes, and section 13 states the difference. The document types and the template codes a treatment type requires are reference rows and list values read at their version, so no type and no code is written in code.
why: The legacy set per treatment type and the legal flag per document type are data owned by Legal and the product owner, and the only way to keep them out of code in the target is the reference-data contract of rwb-case, while the work package fixes the dependency lists of the story.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 3, 8 (BR1, BR3), 11 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 DP-07 and R5.7; context pack S2 (no list table of S2; reference data through rwb-case).
confirm: The P3 contract owner and the solution architect confirm the list and set rows before the wave 2 build start.
impact: Medium: a late contract delays the expected set to a config row, and no criterion changes.

text: SCR-14 Treatment record is the treatment screen and its treatment leg is served by this story's panel; the review view on SCR-30, the correction form and the four write actions are RWB-P5-E2017-APP's and rwb-document's. The two legs are merged by the gateway-bff composite route, one hop each and read only, and the route path, the screen field list and the layout belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the screen owners; the browser calls no owner service directly.
why: The legacy story builds both screens in one module, DP-19 replaces the monolith screen with a composite route, and the work package splits the same screen across two services without saying which leg answers which part of it.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 15; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 8 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s, breaker); work package B2-S2-019.
confirm: RWB-PLT-N001-CON publishes the SCR-14 route and its merge order.
impact: Low: the service side is fixed here and the screen field list is proved against the route fake.

text: This slice publishes no event and registers no Schedule, and both stay in the pattern list as prohibitions: DP-09 is not in the work package's patterns, the service's topic rwb.treatment.events.v1 carries nothing from this key, its catalogue events TreatmentApproved and TreatmentClosed belong to the approval and closure stories, and no job of this capability exists to move to a Temporal Schedule. The section, the log lines and the tests carry identifiers, codes, versions, states, counts and dates only, and never a merge value, a party name, a national ID number, an address or a file byte.
why: A read that writes nothing cannot honestly declare a producer or a schedule, and the events of the service are already owned by other stories of the epic; declaring one here would put an outbox row into a slice that has no write.
read: Architecture v5 slides 18, 42 and 43; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10 and R7.2 s17; legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 12, 16 and 17; context pack S2 (S2 owns one event, EV-10).
applied_in: Story sections 7 (AC8), 12.3, 12.4, 12.6, 13 and 17; fragment events_published and events_consumed
confirm: The event catalogue owner confirms that no event is assigned to the treatment-side panel.
impact: Low: no event and no Schedule means no catalogue change and no chart change.

text: The access guard, the parameters and reference-data client libraries, the decision-record library and the gateway-bff composite route are wave-0 platform and service-template capabilities: this story declares the patterns and the dependency each adds, keeps the work package's lists, and builds against their fakes on Day 1. The capability area 'Treatment and offer', the right R and the scope filter are rwb-access data and this story owns no check of its own. The FSD S2 and TSD S2 module extracts are not present in the run's extract folder, so the business detail is taken from the legacy story and the S2 context pack, and the TSD rows cited are the ones the sibling stories of the same service already cite; no field list is restated from a source that was not read.
why: Every service is built from one template and shared libraries (Architecture v5 slide 20), the platform stories arrive in wave 0, the work package fixes the build list of this story as empty, and the run's extract folder holds no FSD S2 or TSD S2 file although the work package names it as a read.
read: Architecture v5 slides 11, 13 and 20; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; TSD S2 v2 T6.1 and T-A.1 as cited by the sibling stories of RWB-SVC-S2; _work/msr/extract listing of this run.
confirm: The platform template owner confirms the library delivery ahead of wave 2, and the S2 module extract is restored before the contract freeze.
impact: Medium: a missing template capability becomes a platform dependency at build time and a missing extract is a documentation fix, and neither changes a criterion.
